findings.title: describe(reduce='TSNE') crashes with default max_dims (documented model unusable in describe)
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; x = np.random.default_rng(3).normal(size=(50, 15)); hyp.describe(x, reduce='TSNE', show=False)"
findings.expected: A correlation-by-components result for TSNE (docstring: 'Models supported: ... TSNE ...'), or a clear hypertools error saying TSNE only supports up to 3 components in describe.
findings.actual: ValueError: 'n_components' should be inferior to 4 for the barnes_hut algorithm as it relies on quad-tree or oct-tree.

findings.title: reduce(x, 'TSNE') crashes on datasets with <= 30 rows (sklearn default perplexity passed through)
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.default_rng(2).normal(size=(30, 8)), 'TSNE', ndims=2)"
findings.expected: A 2D TSNE embedding, or a hypertools-level message explaining how to lower perplexity via the dict spec.
findings.actual: ValueError: perplexity (30.0) must be less than n_samples (30)

findings.title: reduce docstring 'If the input is a list, a list is returned' is false for single-element lists
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; r = hyp.reduce([np.random.rand(40, 12)], 'PCA', ndims=3); print(type(r))"
findings.expected: <class 'list'> per the docstring (or a corrected docstring).

findings.title: ndims=None (the default) and ndims >= n_features silently return the input unchanged - no reduction, no warning
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; x = np.random.default_rng(2).normal(size=(30, 8)); print(hyp.reduce(x, 'PCA').shape); print(np.array_equal(hyp.reduce(x, 'PCA', ndims=8), x))"
findings.expected: Documented behavior; ideally a UserWarning that the reduction was skipped, or the actual PCA rotation when the user explicitly named a model.
findings.actual: (30, 8) and True - input returned verbatim with no warning.

findings.title: Invalid reduce= spec error: never names the offending value, contains run-on whitespace, and links to hypertools 0.8 docs
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.rand(30, 8), 'umap', ndims=2)"  # then: curl -sIL http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html
findings.expected: Something like: ValueError: unrecognized reduce model 'umap'; did you mean 'UMAP'? Supported: PCA, IncrementalPCA, ... (see <current 1.0 docs URL>).
findings.actual: ValueError: reduce must be one of the supported options or support n_components and fit_transform          methods. See http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html#hypertools.tools.reduce          for supported models  [curl: 200, <title>hypertools.tools.reduce — hypertools 0.8]

findings.title: Canonical dict-spec error message instructs users to use the DEPRECATED 'params' key
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.rand(30, 8), {'kwargs': {'whiten': True}}, ndims=3)"
findings.expected: Error text describing the canonical {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} form.
findings.actual: ValueError: If passing a dictionary, pass the model as the value of the "model" key and a                 dictionary of custom params as the value of the "params" key.

findings.title: Ragged dataset lists (unequal column counts) fail with a raw numpy vstack error
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce([np.random.rand(30, 8), np.random.rand(30, 5)], 'PCA', ndims=3)"
findings.expected: ValueError from hypertools: 'all datasets must have the same number of columns to share one reduction (got 8 and 5)...'
findings.actual: ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly, but along dimension 1, the array at index 0 has size 8 and the array at index 1 has size 5

findings.title: Fitted-Reducer reuse crashes with raw AttributeError for TSNE/MDS/SpectralEmbedding (models without .transform)
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; rng = np.random.default_rng(2); _, m = hyp.reduce(rng.normal(size=(40, 8)), 'TSNE', ndims=2, return_model=True, random_state=0); hyp.reduce(rng.normal(size=(5, 8)), reduce=m)"
findings.expected: A hypertools error naming the limitation and the fix, e.g. 'fitted TSNE models cannot embed new data; call reduce() on the combined data instead' - plus a docstring caveat.
findings.actual: AttributeError: 'TSNE' object has no attribute 'transform'  (same for 'MDS' and 'SpectralEmbedding')

findings.title: describe() docs say it correlates 'covariance'; it actually correlates pairwise Euclidean DISTANCE matrices (and the summary line is ungrammatical)
findings.repro: grep -n 'covariance' /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/reduce/describe.py /Users/jmanning/hypertools/examples/plot_describe.py; env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import inspect; from hypertools.reduce import describe as d; import hypertools.reduce.describe as m; print(inspect.getsource(m.get_cdist))"
findings.expected: Docstring/example text describing correlation of pairwise Euclidean distance matrices.
findings.actual: describe.py:15 'Create plot describing covariance with as a function of number of dimensions'; plot_describe.py:9-11 'computes the covariance (samples by samples)'; code: return cdist(x, x)

findings.title: describe max_dims is an EXCLUSIVE bound: 'Maximum number of dimensions to consider' is off by one
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; r = hyp.describe(np.random.rand(50, 15), max_dims=5, show=False); print(len(r['average']))"
findings.expected: 4 values (dims 2..5) per the docstring wording, or a docstring stating the bound is exclusive.

findings.title: describe() emits the 'When input data is large...' UserWarning unconditionally on every call
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -W always -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.describe(np.random.rand(20, 8), max_dims=5, show=False)"
findings.actual: UserWarning: When input data is large, this computation can take a long time. (fires for a 20x8 array)

findings.title: Multi-dataset describe figure (matplotlib): indistinguishable same-color unlabeled traces, no legend, and the 'average' curve is never plotted; plotly backend differs
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, hypertools as hyp; rng = np.random.default_rng(3); hyp.describe([rng.normal(size=(9, 15)), rng.normal(size=(9, 15))], show=True); plt.gcf().savefig('/tmp/describe_traces.png')"
findings.expected: Distinguishable per-dataset colors + legend (like the plotly backend), and ideally the average curve overlaid.
findings.actual: Two identical-color unlabeled lines; no legend; no average curve (see evidence PNGs).

findings.title: get_corr is called with its arguments in the opposite order of its parameter names
findings.expected: Call-site argument order matching the parameter names.
findings.actual: describe.py:112 'corrs.append(get_corr(alldims, reduced))' vs describe.py:173 'def get_corr(reduced, alldims):'

findings.title: `import hypertools.reduce.reduce as m` fails because the top-level function shadows the subpackage
findings.expected: Either a working import or documentation of the supported import forms.
findings.actual: ImportError: cannot import name 'reduce' from 'reduce' (unknown location)

findings.title: describe() gives no handle on its figure (show-only): cannot save, style, or embed it
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; r = hyp.describe(np.random.rand(40, 10), show=True); print(sorted(r.keys()))"
findings.expected: Some way to obtain the rendered figure (return value or parameter).
findings.actual: ['average', 'individual'] - no figure reference; matplotlib prints 'FigureCanvasAgg is non-interactive, and thus cannot be shown' under Agg.

findings.title: Dependency warnings leak through every MDS/UMAP reduce call (sklearn 1.8 FutureWarnings, umap UserWarning)
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -W always -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.rand(60, 20), 'MDS', ndims=2, random_state=0)"
findings.expected: No FutureWarnings on default usage (pin n_init/init explicitly), keeping MDS results stable across sklearn upgrades.
findings.actual: FutureWarning: The default value of `n_init` will change from 4 to 1 in 1.9. ... | FutureWarning: The default value of `init` will change from 'random' to 'classical_mds' in 1.10. ...

findings.title: Cross-module normalize= with a wrong value fails with an AssertionError that never names the offending value
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.rand(40, 12), reduce='PCA', ndims=3, normalize='zscore')"
findings.expected: ValueError: normalize='zscore' is not recognized; use 'across', 'within', 'row', 'none', or a fitted Normalizer.
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: [infra/release-hygiene] repo .venv contains a stale non-editable hypertools 1.0.0.dev0 whose reduce() still has the fixed dict-spec/ndims bug
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && .venv/bin/pip show hypertools | head -3 && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp, numpy as np; rng = np.random.default_rng(0); a = rng.normal(size=(40, 12)); b = rng.normal(size=(25, 12)); print([r.shape for r in hyp.reduce([a, b], reduce={'model': 'PCA', 'kwargs': {'whiten': True}}, ndims=3)])"
findings.expected: [(40, 3), (25, 3)] (what the repo source on audit/release-1.0-2026-07 produces).
findings.actual: Version: 1.0.0.dev0 (non-editable); output [(40, 12), (25, 12)] - ndims silently ignored by the stale installed copy; traceback paths point at .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/hypertools/.
